messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Private-VPC cross-region routing errors detected for ILB-backed services. Severity: P1. Affected: multiple Private VPC customers in eu-west1 and us-central1. Pager sent to oncall.

anya (oncall): I’m on it — seeing elevated 502s and ILB healthcheck failures in the dashboards. link: https://dd/redwood/dashboards/ilb-routing

datadog-alerts: Alert: Backend 502 spike > 30% for service: inference-rt-eu (avg latency 350ms).

julian (sre): grabbing logs. early hypothesis: route propagation to some worker regions failing, causing backends to be unreachable from ILB.

mike (eng-platform): customers on Dedicated/Private reported sudden cross-region routing — traffic from eu customers hitting us-central1 pools. Confirm?

anya (oncall): yes, support tickets reporting wrong region routing and increased cold-starts. Starting customer-impact triage. Sophia can you get a quick customer list from support queue?

sophia (customer-ops): pulling list now. So far: cust-alpha (EU), cust-beta (EU), cust-gamma (mixed). I'll DM updated list to oncall.

julian (sre): sharing packet capture snippet from one affected host (sanitized):
```
SRC=10.12.45.12 DST=10.32.1.5 proto=TCP dport=443 flags=S
...
```
Seems ILB forwarding rules are pointing at wrong regional backend group.

mike (eng-platform): any recent infra rollouts that touched route propagation or the GCP control-plane client? I pushed the small rollout to infra-agent yesterday but rolled back.

eng-infra: we did a config push related to AGGREGATED_ROUTE_CACHE TTL at 02:00 UTC. Reverted at 02:12 due to unrelated test failure. Could be correlated.

julian (sre): I’m seeing errors in our control-plane logs: 503 from GCP Route Propagation API with body: "rateBackoff: exceededWriteQps". Repeating.

anya (oncall): that would explain transient suppression of updates — ILB still references old backend sets if route table updates were suppressed.

incident-bot: @channel GCP status: "Intermittent rate limiting observed on Route Propagation API in multiple regions" — https://status.cloud.google.com/incidents/route-propagation

mike (eng-platform): contacting GCP support now. Posting case number when available.

gcp-support: Hi team, we see elevated control plane throttles tied to high fanout in the Route Propagation service. Our engineers are throttling write QPS; mitigation options: reduce propagation fanout, apply static regional routes, or request temporary quota increase. We'll escalate. Case# 0123456789.

anya (oncall): immediate mitigation we can do from our side? Options: 1) Pause cross-region rollout traffic via smart routing, 2) revert recent AGGREGATED_ROUTE_CACHE change (we already reverted), 3) create manual static route mapping for the most impacted customers. Thoughts?

julian (sre): quick and lower-risk: adjust surface-level routing policy to prefer regional mirror endpoints we already host in each region (fallback mirror pool). That avoids touching GCP route propagation and keeps ILB forwarding stable.

mike (eng-platform): I can flip the routing policy to regional-prefer in the control plane (takes ~90s to propagate within our control plane). Doing a canary to 5% of GA users now.

anya (oncall): do it. monitor for error reduction and watch for any auth/tooling impacts.

mike (eng-platform): canary complete, 5% -> 100% rollout. Confirming metrics.

datadog-alerts: Alert cleared for inference-rt-eu 502 spike. Backend error rate down to baseline in canary subset.

anya (oncall): good signal. I'll hold on further GCP changes while they investigate. Notify customers impacted that we have mitigation in place and we’re working with GCP for root cause. Sophia please draft a short notice.

sophia (customer-ops): drafting and will send to affected customer contacts within 15 min.

gcp-support: Our control plane team applied a soft quota increase on your project and mitigations to reduce fanout impact. Suggest continuing to avoid large choreography that results in high route write QPS. We'll provide a postmortem.

julian (sre): note for handoff — root cause looks like combined: 1) internal config change that increased route churn (AGGREGATED_ROUTE_CACHE TTL), 2) higher than normal route fanout from ongoing canary rollout, 3) GCP control-plane rate limiting triggering route suppression. Resulted in ILB referencing stale backend groups across regions.

anya (oncall): adding actionable items to incident thread: - do not re-run the global rollout until we confirm GCP fully recovered, - add rate-limiting in our route write client, - implement exponential backoff + batching in infra-agent, - follow up with GCP for quota/architectural guidance.

danielle (oncall-2): taking 2nd shift handoff at 04:00 UTC. Summary for handoff: mitigation applied (regional-prefer routing), GCP raised soft quota, customer notifications underway, monitoring stable but watching for relapse. Please escalate to SRE on-call if error rates > 5% above baseline.

mike (eng-platform): adding immediate monitoring: gcp.route_write_errors, ilb.backend_mismatch_count, smartrouting.fallback_rate. Dashboards updated.

julian (sre): saving logs + timelines for postmortem. Snippet for timeline:
- 02:00 UTC: AGGREGATED_ROUTE_CACHE TTL change pushed
- 02:05 UTC: first increase in route write QPS observed
- 02:12 UTC: config reverted (eng-infra)
- 02:20 UTC: GCP Route Propagation throttling starts
- 02:25 UTC: customers report wrong-region routing / 502s
- 02:32 UTC: oncall pager triggered (P1)
- 02:40 UTC: mitigation (regional-prefer) rolled to 100%
- 03:05 UTC: GCP applied soft quota/mitigation
- 03:45 UTC: metrics stable, incident declared contained

sophia (customer-ops): customers notified. One enterprise customer asked for timeline and potential credit — capture contact and escalate to AM.

anya (oncall): good work. Post-incident action items: (a) add guardrails to infra config pushes that affect route churn, (b) implement client-side batching + backoff for route writes, (c) run a DR test with GCP to confirm our large fanout behavior is tolerated or find alternate design.

incident-bot: Incident severity changed to P2 / contained. Postmortem owner: julian (sre).

danielle (oncall-2): taking point on coordinating postmortem and publishing timeline. I'll create the incident board and runbook updates.

anya (oncall): handing off to danielle and julian. If anything spikes, page SRE and Eng-Platform. Otherwise we’ll reconvene for postmortem in 24h.

julian (sre): will pull GCP case updates and begin draft RCA. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
